reviews.review: This game is too difficult to play with just a few people
This game is so sick. Genuinely one of the best attempts in that genre and the best looking so far.
Incredibly funny horror co-op. Looking forward to future updates!

I've only played for a bit with a friend but I can already really see the game's strengths, I think.

The first and primary strength is a real sense of polish. Other "Lethal-Likes" or extraction looters tend to have a feeling of jankiness to them. This is like, an actual game, with polished animations and physics. Enemies have contextual animation for trying to get at you under a table, for example. and I've seen minimal clipping. The game features a simple but effective hiding spot system that makes it clear what you're supposed to do. The little robot you play as is a really perfect design. It's very obvious when you're hiding and when you're not. And keeping with the physics based nature of the game, upon taking knockback damage (or better yet on command) you turn into a little ball yourself.

The act of looting itself is quite fun, which is good considering that's the entire goal of the game. Finding objects, picking them up, and trying to fit them into your cart is kinda genius game design. To me, throwing open doors and cupboards to find loot inside with mouse movement is always satisfying. 

The lack of time limit and map system remove frustrations I have with other extraction looters. I don't like being under time pressure and I don't like being lost. I also don't like being blind, and so the flashlight not being infinite is a great help. So that means the challenge comes in protecting your loot and avoiding monsters.

Being able to revive your buddy is great and it ties directly into the main loot mechanic because it's tied to how much money you put on extraction. So whenever you extract, you can revive your friends. And of course your friend is a little bobblehead when broken too, tying into the physics system looting aspect.

I think the game has a very strong central mechanic and theme, and builds everything along that central pillar. Like I said before it has polish and has no jankiness, which is a really big selling point IMO, silly as that soudns. 

And that's not even getting into the large amount of upgrades and weapons that I've seen. I've only used really one weapon on one enemy type and it felt like a cool interaction.

That's what it is: It kind of feels like an immersive sim. An extremely simplified one, but with friends online. It feels like quick thinking and using tools to your advantage is rewarded. So yeah, pretty cool!!
